      "papers": [
        {
          "ref_number": 5,
          "title": "Rt-1: Robotics transformer for real-world control at scale.",

          "year": 2022,
          "arxiv_id": "2212.06817",
          "doi": null,
          "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.06817",
          "why_it_matters": "Shows how a transformer trained on millions of heterogeneous demonstrations can generalize across robot platforms, informing how handheld‑gripper data might be incorporated into a universal policy."
        },

          "ref_number": 48,
          "title": "Deep imitation learning for complex manipulation tasks from virtual reality teleoperation",
          "authors": "Tianhao Zhang, Zoe McCarthy, Owen Jow, Dennis Lee, Xi Chen, Ken Goldberg, and Pieter Abbeel.",

          "arxiv_id": "1710.04615",
          "doi": null,
          "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/1710.04615",

        },
        {
          "ref_number": 36,
          "title": "Grasping in the Wild: Learning 6DoF Closed-Loop Grasping From Low-Cost Demonstrations.",
          "authors": "Shuran Song, Andy Zeng, Johnny Lee, and Thomas Funkhouser.",
          "year": 2020,
          "arxiv_id": null,
          "doi": "10.1109/LRA.2020.3004787",
          "url": "https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/9126187",
          "why_it_matters": "Collects low‑cost, handheld‑device demonstrations for grasping and trains policies that transfer to varied robot grippers, exemplifying cross‑embodiment learning."
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "theme": "Policy learning from demonstrations (diffusion, imitation, data quality)",
      "papers": [
        {
          "ref_number": 9,
          "title": "Diffusion policy: Visuomotor policy learning via action diffusion.",
          "authors": "Cheng Chi, Zhenjia Xu, Siyuan Feng, Eric Cousineau, Yilun Du, Benjamin Burchfiel, Russ Tedrake, and Shuran Song.",
          "year": 2023,
          "arxiv_id": null,
          "doi": null,
          "url": null,
          "why_it_matters": "Provides a generative policy framework that can ingest demonstrations from any embodiment and synthesize actions for a target robot, useful for mapping handheld‑gripper trajectories to new end‑effectors."
        },
        {
          "ref_number": 4,
          "title": "Data Quality in Imitation Learning.",
          "authors": "Suneel Belkhale, Yuchen Cui, and Dorsa Sadigh.",
          "year": 2023,
          "arxiv_id": null,
          "doi": null,
          "url": "https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/fe692980c5d9732cf153ce27947653a7-Paper-Conference.pdf",
          "why_it_matters": "Analyzes how noise and bias in demonstration data affect downstream policies, guiding the cleaning and re‑annotation of handheld‑gripper recordings before cross‑embodiment transfer."
        },
        {
          "ref_number": 22,
          "title": "Imitation learning: A survey of learning methods.",
          "authors": "Ahmed Hussein, Mohamed Medhat Gaber, Eyad Elyan, and Chrisina Jayne.",
          "year": 2017,
          "arxiv_id": null,
          "doi": null,
          "url": null,
          "why_it_matters": "Offers a comprehensive taxonomy of imitation‑learning algorithms, helping researchers select approaches (e.g., behavior cloning vs. inverse RL) that are robust to embodiment mismatches."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
